context: Use this bundled 40-company snapshot of the YC Startup Directory; for the seven slugs in the input the directory records (slug, name, batch, location, industries in order): doordash: DoorDash, Summer 2013, San Francisco, CA, USA, [Consumer, Food and Beverage]; instacart: Instacart, Summer 2012, San Francisco, CA, USA, [Consumer, Food and Beverage]; benchling: Benchling, Summer 2012, San Francisco, CA, USA, [B2B]; amplitude: Amplitude, Winter 2012, San Francisco, CA, USA, [B2B, Analytics]; segment: Segment, Summer 2011, San Francisco, CA, USA, [B2B, Analytics]; heap: Heap, Winter 2013, Seattle, WA, USA, [B2B, Analytics]; codecademy: Codecademy, Summer 2011, New York City, NY, USA, [Education]. Build one node per company, per distinct batch, per distinct location, and per distinct industry tag among these companies. Node ids are company:<slug>, batch:<slugified batch>, location:<slugified location>, industry:<slugified tag>; slugify lowercases and replaces every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, e.g. 'Summer 2013' -> 'summer-2013', 'San Francisco, CA, USA' -> 'san-francisco-ca-usa', 'Food and Beverage' -> 'food-and-beverage'. Node names are the company's name, the batch text like 'Summer 2013', the full location text, and the industry tag; kinds are Company, Batch, Location, Industry. Add edges from each company to its batch (IN_BATCH), its location (LOCATED_IN), and each of its industry tags (IN_INDUSTRY). Two companies compete (COMPETES_WITH, from the one earlier in the input to the one later) exactly when both have at least two industry tags and their second tags are equal; a company with one tag competes with no one, and sharing only the first tag is not competing. Every node and edge appears once. Save the graph to graphs/graph.json.
